progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: B6b: mRNA is a single strand of RNA copied from one gene, built 5' to 3' with U in place of T; it leaves the nucleus through pores to ribosomes in the cytoplasm; it is read in codons of three bases; a gene usually codes for a polypeptide, a chain of amino acids that folds into a protein; RNA pairing is A with U and C with G. B4: antiparallel strands with 5' and 3' ends. B6a: mitochondria came from bacteria that began living inside larger cells. Year 11: enzymes, the cytoplasm, rough endoplasmic reticulum. Not assumed: translation, ribosome structure, rRNA, tRNA, anticodon, start and stop codons, peptide bond, the codon chart.
progression.startsWith: An mRNA message written in four bases, proteins built from twenty amino acids, and the question of how the message is read and what acts as the translator.
progression.stopsAfter: Explaining why codons are three bases; describing the ribosome (small and large subunits, protein and rRNA, in the cytoplasm); describing tRNA (one specific amino acid, an anticodon, many kinds loaded by enzymes); writing a directed anticodon for a codon; using the codon chart with mRNA codons; describing start at AUG (methionine), the repeating cycle and stop codons; saying a polypeptide must fold before it works as a protein; assessing the roles of mRNA and tRNA; applying all of it to a DNA template with a chart excerpt and to an antibiotic that makes bacterial ribosomes misread codons. No A, P and E site names, wobble, protein structure levels, mutation types or sedimentation labels.
progression.nextLesson: B07: proteins, phenotype and gene-environment interaction: how the order of amino acids decides a protein's shape and job.

teaching.task: Explain how a ribosome turns a code of four bases into a chain of amino acids, and use the codon chart and a directed anticodon on an unseen sequence.
teaching.causalExplanation: Four bases can name only four amino acids and pairs only sixteen, but triplets give sixty-four, more than enough for twenty, so the code is read in threes. The ribosome holds the mRNA and moves along it one codon at a time but does not choose amino acids; tRNA is the adaptor, with an anticodon that pairs antiparallel with a codon at one end and one particular amino acid, loaded by an enzyme, at the other. The chart is written for mRNA codons. Translation starts at AUG, then each round a matching tRNA arrives, rRNA joins the amino acids with a peptide bond and the ribosome moves one codon, until a stop codon, which no tRNA matches, lets a release protein free the chain. The order of codons sets the order of amino acids, and the polypeptide then has to fold. mRNA sets the order and tRNA makes the code readable, so both are essential.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on the strand leaving the pore and the four-to-twenty puzzle, works out why three bases by counting, builds the ribosome and tRNA one need at a time, keeps ends on every anticodon, runs one four-codon message from start to stop on one board with a chain tally, assesses both RNAs by removing each in turn, gives a stop-codon mnemonic and the language aid, then asks two harder unseen items, each followed by a model answer built one point at a time.
teaching.openingDecision: A message written with four bases has to build a chain made from twenty kinds of amino acid. How does it do that?
teaching.understandingCheck: Given the DNA template 3' TAC TTC GGA ACT 5' and a chart excerpt, write the amino acid sequence (Met, Lys, Pro, with UGA a stop that adds none), explain why there are three amino acids, and write the anticodon for the second amino acid with its ends (3' UUC 5'). Then explain how streptomycin can kill bacteria while the patient's own cytoplasmic ribosomes keep working, and suggest why it can affect mitochondrial ribosomes.
teaching.curriculumScope: Model the process of polypeptide synthesis, including translation, and assess the importance of mRNA and tRNA (Module 5, ACSBL079). Function and phenotype of proteins go to the proteins lesson; A, P and E sites, wobble, mutation types and protein structure levels are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, the painted ribosome flipped in code so the large subunit is on top, the painted cell and bacterium plates, and a coded translation board (terracotta mRNA with B4 jigsaw tiles and amber U, two slots, lilac-grey L-shaped tRNAs with directed anticodon tiles, warm-coloured named amino acid beads, ink peptide bonds that flash amber, a 4 by 4 codon chart filled by the ported lookup). Blue and green are not used.
design.transitionPlan: The strand leaves the painted pore and the camera pushes in; the cell plate crossfades to the flipped ribosome plate; the translation board persists from the ribosome scene to the both-RNAs scene with the givens line holding the worked message; the codon chart and the three-station strip take the board for one scene each; each attempt card clears the aids and its feedback follows at once, turning the card into pictures and model-answer lines; the next chip slides in; scene crossfade with settle.
